name: ranger
description: Ranger is the foreman who never leaves the site. Give him one prompt and walk away — he runs a self-directing senior-engineering loop that never stops and never runs out of work — nothing but you ends a run. A thin lead (spawns agents, manages state, never edits code) drives six model-tiered sub-agents — scout, planner, claims checker, reviewer, implementer, assessor — through survey → triage → plan → claims-check → plan-review → build → review → verify → commit, one local commit per item. Effort is sized to the item: a one-line copy fix costs two agents, a concurrency or migration bug gets the full adversarial pipeline and a mandatory fresh-eyes gate. A cheap claims-check pass opens every source a plan cites before an expensive reviewer is spent, because most revision rounds are citation defects rather than design defects. Scoring weights consequence separately from value, so a wrong figure on a page users act on outranks a cosmetic nit instead of tying with it. The survey maps every tier of the codebase, not just the one with a UI, and learns — domain×lens pairs that come back clean twice go cold. On a maturing codebase it gets pickier rather than stopping: a quality floor that rises as the run matures and never falls, a capped backlog where filing a new item costs dropping one, and a prune pass where killing stale items is the work. Lean stretches are reported in one line, never acted on — standing down is the user's call, and the survey itself is uncapped, dispatching scout team after scout team until it finds work above the floor or has swept every pair. UI items are driven through a real browser as a user would, with a time-boxed fallback ladder when a state can't be reached. `.ranger/FACTS.md` gives every agent the repo's settled ground truth so nothing is re-derived or hallucinated each cycle. Each invocation runs one cycle and returns; keep it going with `/loop /ranger:run` (watched, Esc to stop) or the bundled headless runner (overnight). Curated `--preset` briefs (ui, ux, a11y, harden, perf) focus the sweep and skip anything the app lacks instead of inventing it, and `--dry-run` previews the work without changing anything. A PreToolUse hook hard-denies git push, remote mutation, and PR creation regardless of what the model decides. Local commits only. Branches and dev merges require explicit flags. Never asks the user anything unless --ask. Blast-radius circuit breaker, no-progress quarantine, and revert-don't-pile-on regression discipline keep an unattended run from turning into churn.
